hr.question: Can I wear a turban or hijab at the office?
hr.reference: Yes. TechCorp Solutions respects and accommodates religious and cultural dress requirements, including head coverings (hijab, turban, kippah). Contact HR for any accommodation needs.

hr.question: Are tattoos and piercings allowed at work?
hr.reference: Tattoos and piercings are generally acceptable. Employees should maintain a neat, clean appearance and keep fragrances subtle.

hr.question: Is the dress code relaxed during extreme weather?
hr.reference: Extreme weather may warrant a relaxed dress code; HR will communicate any temporary changes. Theme days are occasional and voluntary.

hr.question: How long does a harassment investigation usually take?
hr.reference: Investigations are typically completed within 30 days; complex cases may take longer, and the reporting party gets updates throughout.

hr.question: Can I be punished for taking part in a harassment investigation?
hr.reference: No. Retaliation against anyone who reports harassment or participates in an investigation is strictly prohibited and will result in discipline up to termination.

hr.question: How often must employees complete harassment prevention training?
hr.reference: All employees take annual harassment prevention training; managers get additional training on handling complaints, and new hires are trained within the first 30 days.

hr.question: When do I need a doctor's note for being ill?
hr.reference: Notify your manager by 9:00 AM on the day of absence; a medical certificate is required for absences of 3 or more consecutive days.

hr.question: Do adoptive parents get the same leave as birth parents?
hr.reference: Yes. Adoption leave gives the same benefits as biological parents and begins on the date of placement or legal adoption.

hr.question: How many floating holidays are there and how do I use them?
hr.reference: Employees get 2 floating holidays per year for religious observances or personal celebrations, requested at least 1 week in advance.

hr.question: Which jobs cannot be done remotely?
hr.reference: Positions requiring on-site presence: Facilities Management, IT Hardware Support, Reception/Front Desk and Physical Security.

hr.question: Do I have to use the VPN when working from a cafe?
hr.reference: Yes. Use the company VPN for all work activities and never work on public WiFi without the VPN; lock your computer when stepping away.

hr.question: Is there a trial period for a new remote arrangement?
hr.reference: New remote arrangements include a 90-day trial period; remote privileges may be modified or revoked if performance declines.

hr.question: Do I have to pay back my signing bonus if I leave after 8 months?
hr.reference: Leaving within 6 months requires 100% repayment of the signing bonus, 6-12 months 50%, and after 12 months nothing.

hr.question: How much is a retention bonus and how is it paid?
hr.reference: Retention bonuses are typically 10-25% of annual salary, paid in installments over 12-24 months under a signed retention agreement.

hr.question: What reward do I get when my patent is granted?
hr.reference: Patent awards: $1,500 when the application is filed, $3,500 when the patent is granted, and an additional $2,000 if it is used in a product.

hr.question: What is the nightly hotel limit when traveling to New York?
hr.reference: The nightly lodging limit is $350 in major cities (NYC, SF, London), $250 in other US cities, and market rate with pre-approval internationally.

hr.question: How much can I spend per person on a client dinner?
hr.reference: Per person limits: business meal $100, team dinner $75, client event $150, sporting event or show $200 with Director approval.

hr.question: What should I do if I lost a receipt?
hr.reference: Complete a Missing Receipt Affidavit with manager approval; a pattern of missing receipts may result in denied expenses.

hr.question: Is my salary lower if I live in Denver instead of San Francisco?
hr.reference: Yes. Denver is a Tier 3 location paid at 90% of the San Francisco baseline (Tier 1 = 100%).

hr.question: How big is the pay increase when I get promoted?
hr.reference: A typical promotion increase is 10-15%, moving you into the salary band of the new level, effective on the promotion date.

hr.question: Which deductions are taken from my paycheck?
hr.reference: Mandatory deductions are federal and state income tax, Social Security (FICA) and Medicare; voluntary deductions include health premiums, 401(k), HSA/FSA, life insurance and commuter benefits.

hr.question: If my company pays for my master's degree, how long must I stay?
hr.reference: Service commitment: up to $5,000 means 1 year, $5,001-$10,000 means 2 years, over $10,000 means 3 years; leaving earlier requires pro-rated repayment.

hr.question: Will the company pay for Spanish classes?
hr.reference: Yes. Rosetta Stone is free for all languages and language classes are reimbursed up to $1,000 per year.

hr.question: What extra support do I get for speaking at a conference?
hr.reference: Speakers get full conference expenses covered, an additional $500 preparation stipend and an extra PTO day for preparation.

hr.question: Can my 24-year-old son be on my medical plan?
hr.reference: Yes. Eligible dependents include children under age 26 (biological, adopted or step-children), a legal spouse or domestic partner, and disabled adult children.

hr.question: How long can I keep my health coverage after leaving the company?
hr.reference: Through COBRA you can continue coverage for up to 18 months (36 for certain events), paying the full premium plus a 2% administrative fee; elect within 60 days.

hr.question: Can I change my medical plan after getting married?
hr.reference: Yes. Marriage is a qualifying life event; changes are allowed within 30 days of the event.

hr.question: After two years how much of the employer match is vested?
hr.reference: After 2 years of service 50% of the employer match is vested (25% per year, 100% after 4 years); your own contributions are always 100% vested.

hr.question: Can I borrow money from my retirement account?
hr.reference: Yes. You can borrow up to 50% of your vested balance, from $1,000 to a maximum of $50,000, at prime rate + 1%.

hr.question: Can I move my old employer's plan into the TechCorp plan?
hr.reference: Yes. You may roll over funds from previous employer 401(k) plans, traditional IRAs and 403(b) plans.

hr.question: Are flu shots free for employees?
hr.reference: Yes. Free flu shots are offered at all office locations in the fall, and flu shots obtained elsewhere are reimbursed.

hr.question: Does TechCorp help with emergency savings?
hr.reference: Yes. A payroll deduction feeds an emergency savings account and TechCorp matches the first $500 saved (one-time).

hr.question: Is there any support for employees caring for elderly parents?
hr.reference: Elder care resources are available through the EAP, with 5 days per year of subsidized backup elder care and caregiver support groups.

hr.question: What documents should I bring on my first day?
hr.reference: Bring a government-issued photo ID for I-9 verification, a Social Security card or passport, and a voided check for direct deposit.

hr.question: What equipment will I receive when I start?
hr.reference: New hires receive a laptop (MacBook Pro or Dell XPS), a monitor if in-office or hybrid, keyboard and mouse, a headset, an employee badge and a welcome kit.

hr.question: What number do I call for an IT emergency?
hr.reference: IT Emergency: +1 (555) 123-4567 ext. 800. Security is ext. 911 and urgent HR matters go to hr-urgent@techcorp-solutions.com.

hr.question: Can my probation be extended?
hr.reference: Probation may be extended by up to 30 days if performance is borderline or more time is needed; it requires HR approval and written notification.

hr.question: Can I appeal if I am let go during probation?
hr.reference: There is no formal appeal process during probation; probationary employees may request a meeting with HR, and at-will employment applies.

hr.question: How is probation different for someone hired to work remotely?
hr.reference: Remote new hires get more frequent video check-ins, a virtual onboarding buddy and an on-site visit if possible; they are assessed on responsiveness, participation, output quality and self-management.

hr.question: What compliance courses are due every December?
hr.reference: By December 31 each year: Security Awareness Refresher, Anti-Harassment Refresher, Data Privacy Update and Code of Conduct Acknowledgment.

hr.question: Can I get a work book paid for without approval?
hr.reference: Yes. Any work-related book under $50 needs no approval, in physical or Kindle format; books become company property.

hr.question: What must I do after attending a conference?
hr.reference: Share learnings with the team, add them to the knowledge base, and file the expense report within 30 days.
